land.text: the western Greater Polish lands given to Mieszko III by Bolesław III's testament

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Established: 1138'; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1138. Gniezno and Kalisz, 'eastern Greater Poland', went to the Seniorate in 1138 and were won by Mieszko III only in 1181.

land.text: the part of Greater Poland that Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape of 1305 covers (97 of the 111 cells)

successors.note: Wenceslaus II of Bohemia, to whom the Piasts 'were compelled to renounce their claims' in 1300, died in 1305 and 'the rivalry resumed' (Greater Poland page); Władysław I the Elbow-high's kingdom (crowned 1320) takes the land.

land.text: 11 cells in the south-west that Cliopatria gives to Głogów in 1305

successors.note: The Greater Poland page's ruler table lists Henry III of Głogów for 1305-1309 (row '1306').

capitals.name: Poznań
capitals.note: Infobox capital Poznań. Gniezno and Kalisz were the other two principalities when the duchy was 'internally divided into Poznań, Gniezno and Kalisz: 1191-1194, 1207-1229, 1234-1238, 1247-1250, 1253-1257, 1277-1279' (infobox); no page opened dates a move of the capital. Coordinates are the city's, not from the page.

rulers.name: Mieszko III the Old
rulers.note: Duke of Greater Poland from 1138 and High Duke 1173-1177, 1191, 1198-1199; died 13 March 1202. His son Odon held Poznań 1177-1194 ('Poznań, held by Odon 1177-1194, by Władysław III 1194-1202').

rulers.name: Władysław III Spindleshanks
rulers.note: Infobox 'Duke of Greater Poland 1202-1229'; High Duke 1202-1206 and 1228-1229. His nephew Odonic held the south from 1216 (Gniezno and Poznań 1216-1217).

rulers.name: Władysław Odonic
rulers.note: Infobox 'Duke of Greater Poland 1229-1239 (only the northern part from 1234)'; died 5 June 1239.

rulers.name: Przemysł I
rulers.note: 'Because Bolesław was a minor when Władysław Odonic died on 5 June 1239, his elder brother Przemysł I ruled alone at first'; Bolesław the Pious shared the duchy from 1241 and held Gniezno-Kalisz 1253-1257; Przemysł I died 4 June 1257. Henry I the Bearded and Henry II the Pious held parts 1234-c.1243.

rulers.name: Bolesław the Pious
rulers.note: Infobox 'Duke of Greater Poland 1257-1279'; died 14 April 1279 at Kalisz. Przemysł II was independent Duke of Poznań from 1273.

rulers.name: Przemysł II
rulers.note: Duke of Greater Poland 1279-1296, High Duke at Kraków 1290-1291, King of Poland 1295-1296; murdered 8 February 1296.

rulers.name: Władysław I the Elbow-high
rulers.note: Ruler table row 1296-1300; 'In 1300, both Piasts were compelled to renounce their claims in favor of King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia'.

rulers.name: Wenceslaus II of Bohemia
rulers.note: He died in 1305; the Greater Poland page's table then lists Henry III of Głogów (1305-1309).

ledger.note: 1198: Mieszko III returns to Kraków as High Duke. 'In 1198, he was finally allowed to return to Lesser Poland.'

region.text: Kraków and the Seniorate Province [without Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia cells, which the Masovia dossier draws for 1173-1176 and 1227-1229]

ledger.note: 1199: Leszek the White is restored at Kraków. The page: Mieszko was 'again deposed' in 1199 and Leszek 'restored ... as high duke'; 'Mieszko III died in 1202, still holding authority in Greater Poland'. Who held Kraków in 1200-1201 is not on the pages opened (the Sandomierz row of Cliopatria says Casimir's heirs, to 1201).

region.text: the Kuyavia region annexed in 1186

ledger.note: 1199: Kuyavia leaves Greater Poland. 'Mieszko was compelled to cede it to Duke Konrad of Masovia, son of Casimir II, in 1199' (Duchy of Greater Poland page); the Mieszko III page puts the cession to 'Casimir's sons' in 1198, and the Konrad I page has Konrad receive Masovia in 1199 and 'the adjacent lands of Kuyavia as well' in 1205. Reading shared with the Masovia dossier (ledger 6-7): the land passes in 1199 to Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia row (1188-1205), which holds it until Konrad's 1205 gain; the 1199 date is this page's, the pages do not name a holder for 1199-1205.

region.text: Kraków and the Seniorate Province [without Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia cells, which the Masovia dossier draws for 1173-1176 and 1227-1229]

ledger.note: 1202: Władysław III Spindleshanks becomes Duke of Kraków and High Duke. 'Mieszko III died on 13 March 1202'; 'Władysław's rule as Duke of Kraków and High Duke of Poland lasted for four years, until 1206' (infobox 'Reign: 1202-1206'). The page gives the year, the land is the Seniorate by reading.

region.text: Kraków and the Seniorate Province [without Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia cells, which the Masovia dossier draws for 1173-1176 and 1227-1229]

ledger.note: 1206: Spindleshanks loses Kraków to Leszek the White. 'until 1206, when, after the death of his principal supporter voivode Mikołaj Gryfita', Leszek returned (Greater Poland page: 'In 1206, Władysław III Spindleshanks lost the high ducal title to Leszek I the White').

region.text: the Duchy of Kalisz, southern Greater Poland round Kalisz

ledger.note: 1207: Kalisz is split off for Władysław Odonic. 'in 1207, Henry I the Bearded gave to Władysław Odonic the Duchy of Kalisz' (Spindleshanks: 'Duke of Kalisz 1202-1206'; infobox of Odonic 'Duke of Kalisz 1207-1217'). Cliopatria's Duchy of Kalisz row begins in 1210.

region.text: the Duchy of Kalisz

ledger.note: 1217: Kalisz returns to Spindleshanks' Greater Poland. Odonic's infobox: 'Duke of Kalisz 1207-1217'; the same year Leszek the White and Spindleshanks concluded a treaty (Spindleshanks page). The page does not say who took Kalisz; Cliopatria's Kalisz row runs to 1219.

region.text: Kraków and the Seniorate Province [without Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia cells, which the Masovia dossier draws for 1173-1176 and 1227-1229]

ledger.note: 1228: Spindleshanks is elected High Duke at Wiślica. 'The formal election of the new High Duke of Poland was made at a meeting in Wiślica on 5 May 1228' (infobox 'Reign: 1228-1229'); Leszek the White had been killed on 24 November 1227. The Seniorate is the land by reading.

region.text: Kraków and the Seniorate Province [without Cliopatria's Duchy of Kuyavia cells, which the Masovia dossier draws for 1173-1176 and 1227-1229]

ledger.note: 1229: Spindleshanks loses the Seniorate to Konrad I of Masovia and Greater Poland to Odonic. Infobox 'Reign: 1228-1229'; 'In 1229, Władysław Odonic and Konrad I of Masovia took a concerted action against Władysław III Spindleshanks' (Odonic page); Konrad 'assumed the title of a Polish High Duke in 1229' (Konrad I page). Spindleshanks fled to Casimir I of Opole and died on 3 November 1231.

region.text: the territories south and west of the Warta River, including Kalisz

ledger.note: 1234: Henry I the Bearded of Silesia invades Greater Poland. 'In the summer of 1234, Henry the Bearded decided to re-intervene in Greater Poland.'

region.text: the territories south and west of the Warta River, including Kalisz

ledger.note: 22 September 1234: the settlement ends the war. 'The terms of the agreement, published on 22 September 1234, were very unfavorable for Władysław Odonic.'

region.text: the territories south and west of the Warta River, including Kalisz

ledger.note: 22 September 1234: Odonic gives up the south. He 'had to relinquish all the territories south and west of the Warta River, which included Kalisz' to Henry I the Bearded (the Henry I page: 'he received the half of Greater Poland up to the Warta River, from Kalisz and Poznań'; the two pages differ on Poznań).

region.text: Odonic's rump north of the Warta round Poznań and Gniezno (Cliopatria's 1236 shape), without Ujście and Nakło

ledger.note: 5 June 1239: Odonic dies and Henry II the Pious takes the rest of Greater Poland. 'When Henry I was succeeded by his son Henry II the Pious in 1238, ... Odonic was reduced to controlling only the area around Ujście. He died the following year, after which High Duke Henry II assumed control over all of Greater Poland' (Duchy of Greater Poland page). The Odonic page: 'In 1239, a new war broke out and once again, Władysław was defeated. This time, he lost the rest of Greater Poland, with the exception of Ujście and Nakło' and 'died on 5 June 1239' (a footnote: later historians hold that he lost Ujście and Nakło in 1239 but 'remained in Gniezno and Poznań until his death'). Drawn: the 1236 rump goes to Silesia; Ujście and Nakło stay with Odonic's sons (the Przemysł I page: the district 'included Ujście and Nakło'). Mirrors duchy-of-silesia ledger 19 (5 June 1239).

region.text: Greater Poland as the brothers hold it from 1250 (Poznań, Gniezno, Kalisz, Santok): what Odonic's sons had to win back from the Silesian successors of Henry II the Pious

ledger.note: 1241: Przemysł I and Bolesław the Pious begin to win back what their father lost. 'In 1241, Przemysł and Boleslaw began reclaiming the lands their father had lost.' The page does not name the holder; Henry I the Bearded and Henry II the Pious of Silesia held it after Odonic (Odonic page). Zone widened to the whole 1250 shape: the 1236 rump itself was lost to Henry II on 5 June 1239 (previous ledger entry).

region.text: most of the Duchies of Poznań and Gniezno, the 1236 rump included (Kalisz still outside)

ledger.note: 1243: the brothers hold most of Poznań and Gniezno again. 'By 1243 the brothers regained most of the Duchies of Poznań and Gniezno.' The holder they took them from is Silesia by reading. The region includes the 1236 rump (Poznań, Gniezno), which Odonic's sons lost on 5 June 1239 (ledger above); the Przemysł I page: 'Przemysł recovered Poznań and Gniezno' and 'In 1242 Przemysł I reconquered Zbąszyń and Międzyrzecz from Bolesław II the Bald'.

region.text: Kalisz and its district (Cliopatria's Duchy of Kalisz row)

ledger.note: 1244: Kalisz is regained. 'in 1244 Kalisz' (Bolesław the Pious' infobox: 'Duke of Kalisz 1244-1249 with Przemysł I').

region.text: Santok, on the Noteć-Warta frontier

ledger.note: 1247: Santok is regained from the Silesian line of Henry II the Pious. 'The actions against the sons of Henry II the Pious were completed in 1247 when Santok was recovered' (Przemysł I page); the Bolesław the Pious page: 'in 1247 Santok'. Santok was among the territories Odonic relinquished to Henry I in 1234 ('Kalisz, Santok, Międzyrzecz, and Śrem', Odonic page). The Silesia dossier has no matching 1247 loss.

region.text: Wieluń

ledger.note: 1249: Wieluń is won. 'in 1249 Wieluń' (Bolesław the Pious page: 'Wieluń, which had recently been returned to the rule of Władysław Odonic's sons'); the Przemysł I page: 'He failed however in his attempt to recover Wieluń, which was only annexed to Greater Poland in 1249'. The holder is by reading: the Wieluń page says it was 'ruled by the Dukes of Silesia from the Duchy of Opole' after 1217 (no 1249 sentence), and the Przemysł I page has Przemysł recover Kalisz 'from Duke Władysław of Opole'. No page gives a loss: the Wieluń page has it 'in the second half of the 13th century ... in Duchy of Greater Poland', the castellany moved there in 1281 and the 'Land of Wieluń' is named by 1299, so it is drawn in the keyframes to 1304. Cliopatria draws these 9 cells under Sandomierz (1250-1278) and Duchies of Poland (1279-1304).

region.text: Greater Poland as the brothers hold it from 1250 (Poznań, Gniezno, Kalisz, Santok)

ledger.note: 1249: the reconquest is complete. Wieluń in 1249 is the last gain listed; Bolesław is 'Duke of Gniezno 1249-1250' and Cliopatria shows the whole duchy again from 1250.

region.text: Santok and its district

ledger.note: 1265: Brandenburg takes Santok. 'In early 1265 Brandenburg occupied the main city of Santok.'

region.text: the Noteć-Warta country round Drezdenko that Cliopatria gives to Brandenburg in 1272 (Santok's 8 cells already lost in 1265, the 8 cells of Deutsch Krone kept until 1296)

ledger.note: 1270: Brandenburg takes Drezdenko. 'The latter was captured by Brandenburg in 1270.' Cliopatria's Margraviate of Brandenburg holds the 35 cells from 1272. The Wałcz (Deutsch Krone) cells that Cliopatria gives to Brandenburg in 1272 are not part of this loss: the Margraviate of Brandenburg page dates their annexation to 1296 (ledger below).

region.text: Poznań, Gniezno and Kalisz under one duke

ledger.counterpart: Duchy of Kalisz and Gniezno (Bolesław the Pious)
ledger.note: 1279: Przemysł II reunites Greater Poland. 'Greater Poland was once again reunited under the rule of Przemysł II, son of Przemysł I, in Poznań in 1279' (infobox 'Re-united under Przemysł II: 1279'; Bolesław the Pious died on 14 April 1279 at Kalisz and Przemysł II 'obtained the Duchy of Kalisz').

region.text: the Duchy of Kraków, 'Kraków and the surrounding areas'

ledger.note: 1290: Przemysł II inherits Kraków. 'Unexpectedly, in 1290, under the will of Henry Probus, he managed to obtain the Duchy of Kraków' (Henry Probus died on 23 June 1290; 'the first time he appeared with the title of Duke of Kraków was in a diploma issued on 25 July 1290').

region.text: the Duchy of Kraków

ledger.note: 1290: Przemysł II gives Kraków up to Wenceslaus II. He 'left Kraków, capital of Lesser Poland, between 12 September and 23 October 1290' and a synod 'decided to abandon his rights over Lesser Poland to Wenceslaus II in exchange for a monetary compensation'; Wenceslaus used the title from 10 April 1291. Przemysł II is listed 'High Duke of Poland 1290-1291'.

region.text: Gdańsk Pomerania (Pomerelia)

ledger.note: December 1294: Przemysł II inherits Gdańsk Pomerania. 'After the death of Duke Mestwin II in 1294, and according to the Treaty of Kępno signed in 1282' (15 February 1282), Mestwin died on 25 December 1294 in Gdańsk; lead: 'Gdańsk Pomerania (Pomerelia) from 1294 to 1296'. Not in the Cliopatria 1294 shape: Cliopatria draws Pomerelia under its Duchies of Poland row.

26 June 1295: Przemysł II is crowned King of Poland at Gniezno. 'The ceremony was held on 26 June 1295 in Gniezno'; infobox 'Reign: 1295-1296 (King of Poland)'. Greater Poland is the core of the restored kingdom until his death.

region.text: Deutsch Krone (Wałcz) and its district: the part of the 1260-1272 Neumark step within 25 km of Wałcz (8 cells)

ledger.note: 1296: Brandenburg annexes Deutsch Krone. 'he lost the town Deutsch Krone (Wałcz), annexed from Greater Poland by Brandenburg in 1296' (Margraviate of Brandenburg page). Cliopatria already gives these cells to Brandenburg in 1272; this dossier follows the page and holds them to 1295 (the Brandenburg dossier's 1272 gain, ledger 3, overlaps them until 1296; its ledger 5 is the mirror of this event).

8 February 1296: Przemysł II is murdered at Rogoźno and the Greater Polish Piast line ends. 'on 8 February 1296, Przemysł II was murdered during a failed kidnapping attempt'; 'the Greater Polish Piast line became extinct ... when Przemysł II was abducted and assassinated' (Greater Poland page), whose ruler table then lists Władysław I the Elbow-high for 1296-1300.

region.text: Gdańsk Pomerania (Pomerelia)

ledger.note: 1296: Gdańsk Pomerania passes out of Greater Poland's hands. The lead gives Przemysł II's rule of Pomerelia as 'from 1294 to 1296'; the pages opened do not say who took it.

region.text: the Międzyrzecz (Meseritz) castellany: Brandenburg's 1305 shape minus its 1272 shape (3 cells)

ledger.note: 1297: Brandenburg annexes the Międzyrzecz castellany. 'the Międzyrzecz castellany, annexed from Greater Poland by Brandenburg in 1297' (Margraviate of Brandenburg page). Mirrors the Brandenburg dossier's ledger 6. The dissolve's 'Brandenburg, 3 cells' successor entry is this land: they were already Brandenburg's from 1297, so the 1304 handover is the Cliopatria boundary only.

region.text: Greater Poland as it stands in 1299: Cliopatria's 1294 shape with Wieluń, without the Międzyrzecz castellany

ledger.note: 1300: the Piasts yield Greater Poland to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. 'In 1300, both Piasts were compelled to renounce their claims in favor of King Wenceslaus II of Bohemia'; 'After Wenceslaus died in 1305, the rivalry resumed' (Duchy of Greater Poland page). Mirrors kingdom-of-bohemia ledger 8 (1300 gain, 'occupied in early 1300') and its ledger 10 (the hold ends in 1306): the Bohemia dossier draws Greater Poland for 1300-1305, so this dossier draws nothing for those years. Cliopatria keeps its Greater Poland shape to 1304; the 1300-1304 years of that shape are not used here.

region.text: Greater Poland as Cliopatria draws it in its last year

ledger.note: 1304: last year of the Cliopatria shape; the land passes to the Kingdom of Poland, Głogów and Brandenburg. The page gives no 1304 event: Wenceslaus II (who held Greater Poland from 1300, previous ledger entries) died in 1305, 'the rivalry resumed', and the ruler table lists Henry III of Głogów for 1305-1309 ('1306 | Henry III of Głogów'). The Władysław I the Elbow-high page: in 1306 'the rest of the duchy had accepted the rule of his old enemy Henry III of Głogów' while Władysław held only Konin, Koło and Nakło; 'By 1311, Władysław was in power in Lesser Poland and his Kuyavian patrimony' and 'Three years later, Greater Poland also came under his rule' (1314, by that sentence's 'Three years later'). The 3 Brandenburg cells were Brandenburg's from 1297. The year 1304 is a map boundary, not a page date.

wars.name: Rebellion against Mieszko III and Casimir II's seizure of Kraków
wars.outcome: Casimir II took Kraków in 1177 (and Gniezno and Kalisz until Mieszko III won them back in 1181) while Mieszko's son Odon held Poznań and fought his father for almost two years.
wars.note: 'withdrew to Poznań, where he stayed for almost two years, enduring heavy fighting with his son Odon' (Casimir II page); the Mieszko III page dates Odon's rebellion to 1177 and the Greater Poland page his expelling his father to 1179.

wars.name: War for the Seniorate (Mozgawa)
wars.outcome: Mieszko III against the heirs of Casimir II (Leszek the White, his successor as High Duke, and the regency of Masovia): the battle of Mozgawa on 13 September 1195; in 1198 Mieszko returned to Kraków and ceded Kuyavia; deposed again in 1199.

wars.name: Spindleshanks-Odonic war
wars.outcome: Odonic took Ujście in October 1223 and Nakło in 1225, defeated his uncle in 1227 and, with Konrad I of Masovia, took all Greater Poland in 1229; Spindleshanks fled to Opole.
wars.note: Civil war inside the duchy: no outer border moved.

wars.name: Henry the Bearded's Greater Polish war

zones.text: the territories south and west of the Warta River, including Kalisz

wars.outcome: Henry I the Bearded intervened in the summer of 1234; the terms published on 22 September 1234 made Odonic relinquish everything south and west of the Warta, Kalisz included.
wars.note: The Henry I page gives the line as the Warta 'from Kalisz and Poznań' and says Henry then gave Kalisz to Odonic except Poznań; the pages differ.

wars.name: Henry II the Pious's war on Władysław Odonic

zones.text: Odonic's rump north of the Warta round Poznań and Gniezno (Cliopatria's 1236 shape), without Ujście and Nakło

wars.outcome: Henry II the Pious (High Duke after Henry I's death on 19 March 1238) defeated Odonic in 1239; Odonic died on 5 June 1239 and Henry II took the rest of Greater Poland, leaving Odonic's sons Ujście and Nakło.
wars.note: 'In 1239, a new war broke out and once again, Władysław was defeated.' The Duchy of Greater Poland page puts the reduction to Ujście in 1238 and Henry II's control of 'all of Greater Poland' after Odonic's death.

wars.name: Reconquest of Greater Poland by Przemysł I and Bolesław the Pious

zones.text: Poznań, Gniezno, Kalisz, Santok and Wieluń

wars.outcome: From 1241 the brothers regained most of Poznań and Gniezno by 1243, Kalisz in 1244, Santok in 1247 and Wieluń in 1249. [The Przemysł I page: the actions against the sons of Henry II the Pious were completed in 1247 with Santok; Międzyrzecz retaken in 1242.]

wars.name: Brandenburg's conquest of Santok and Drezdenko
wars.outcome: Brandenburg occupied Santok in early 1265 and captured Drezdenko in 1270; Cliopatria shows the loss from 1272.

wars.name: Przemysł II's Kraków succession
wars.outcome: Henry Probus willed Kraków to Przemysł II in 1290; he left in September-October 1290 and a synod gave Lesser Poland to Wenceslaus II for compensation.
wars.note: 'This alliance was anti-Bohemian, and his goal was to recover Kraków, then in the hands of King Wenceslaus II' (1293).

wars.name: Greater Polish succession (1296-1300)
wars.outcome: After Przemysł II's murder the Greater Polish Piast line ended; Władysław I the Elbow-high took over (1296-1300) and in 1300 both Piasts renounced their claims in favour of Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. The Margraviate of Brandenburg page dates Brandenburg's annexations from Greater Poland to 1296 and 1297; the Bohemia dossier has Wenceslaus II occupy Greater Poland in early 1300.
wars.note: Pages opened give no fighting or border change inside the 1300-1304 years.

wars.name: Brandenburg's annexation of Deutsch Krone and Międzyrzecz
wars.outcome: Brandenburg annexed Deutsch Krone in 1296 and the Międzyrzecz castellany in 1297 from Greater Poland.
wars.note: The page describes annexations, not fighting.

certainty.note: A duchy of castellany districts: no page opened gives a surveyed or treaty boundary of the duchy as a whole. The one line a treaty names is the Warta in the settlement of 22 September 1234 (and the page itself is unsure about Poznań); Brandenburg's frontier on the Noteć and Warta from 1265-1270 and the Pomeranian frontier are approximate.

sources.title: Przemysł I of Greater Poland

sources.title: Wieluń
sources.note: Repair pass: Wieluń 'ruled by the Dukes of Silesia from the Duchy of Opole', 'in the second half of the 13th century, was in Duchy of Greater Poland', castellany moved to Wieluń in 1281, Land of Wieluń by 1299; no loss date.

sources.title: Władysław I the Elbow-high
sources.note: Repair pass: silent on who took Pomerelia in 1296; 'the rest of the duchy had accepted the rule of his old enemy Henry III of Głogów' (1306), 'Three years later [after 1311], Greater Poland also came under his rule' (1314).

notes: eu-15-d, Duchy of Greater Poland. 14 Cliopatria shapes (1139-1304) all reviewed with nine pages; the infobox gives no area, so no area comparison was possible. Cliopatria's three 'Seniorate' shapes (1177-1187, 1202-1205, 1227-1235; 499, 468 and 498 cells, 116-117 thousand km2) are the High Duke's realm: the page-based owners are Mieszko III (1173-1177, with a gap in Cliopatria which gives these years to Masovia), Casimir II (1177-1191, 1191-1194), Spindleshanks (1202-1206, 1228-1229), Konrad I of Masovia (1229-1232) and Henry I the Bearded (1232-1238, Silesia). So _1177 and _1227 are 'wrong' as Greater Poland shapes and are replaced by Poznań-district shapes; the Seniorate years that are really Greater Poland's (1173-1176, 1228) are new keyframes, and 1202-1205 is ok. The Sandomierz dossier (eu-15-e) agrees on 1177, 1198, 1206 and 1227 but records a 1199 Mieszko return and a 1227 hand-over at confidence 1 that this dossier does not (the Mieszko III page says only that Mieszko was deposed in 1199; Spindleshanks' Kraków begins 1202 and in 1228). Disagreements between pages: Odon's expulsion of his father 1177 (Mieszko III, Casimir II) versus 1179 (Greater Poland page, which also gives 1181 and 1177 for the Gniezno-Kalisz subdivision); Kuyavia ceded 1198 to Casimir's sons (Mieszko III) versus 1199 to Konrad (Greater Poland); Odonic's Kalisz to 1217 (infobox) versus Cliopatria's Kalisz row to 1219; whether Odonic kept Poznań and Gniezno to 1239 (footnote) or lost them to Henry II the Pious (Bolesław the Pious: 'regained most of the Duchies of Poznań and Gniezno' by 1243); the Henry I page puts Poznań on Henry's side of the 1234 Warta line while the Odonic page leaves Poznań to Odonic. The Henry I page is silent on 1238-1239, but the Duchy of Greater Poland and Odonic pages are not (see the repair paragraph). Events at confidence 1: 1304 (dissolve). Not drawn but on the pages: Gdańsk Pomerania 1294-1296 and Kraków 1290-1291 (ledger events; Cliopatria draws Pomerelia under its Duchies of Poland row and Kraków under its Grand Duchy of Kraków row, so the 1294 and 1290 events must not be applied on top of those rows without the colour agent's decision); Lubusz Land to Brandenburg 1248 (the Greater Poland page: 'acquired Lubusz Land ... from Duke Bolesław II Rogatka in 1248', not Greater Poland's loss); the Statute of Kalisz 1264; the 1250-1253 and 1253-1257 internal division of Przemysł I and Bolesław. [Repair 2026-10-31: 1300 is now a loss to kingdom-of-bohemia, matching Bohemia's ledger 8; this dossier draws nothing for 1300-1304.] Counterparts needing dossiers: Duchy of Pomerelia (Mestwin II), the Kuyavian line of Casimir I (1233-1267) is not in Cliopatria. Names the gazetteer lacks: Kalisz, Santok, Drezdenko, Wieluń, Ujście, Nakło (Kalisz is taken from Cliopatria's Duchy of Kalisz row; Santok is a 30 km circle at 15.37E 52.74N intersected with Brandenburg's 1272 gain, Wieluń a 25 km circle at 18.57E 51.22N; the coordinates are the towns', not from the pages). REPAIR PASS 2026-10-31 (reviewer fixes, pages reopened): (1) 1239/6 loss of the 1236 rump to Silesia added (Duchy of Greater Poland page: 'Odonic was reduced to controlling only the area around Ujście. He died the following year, after which High Duke Henry II assumed control over all of Greater Poland'; Odonic page: died 5 June 1239); keyframe 1236 now ends 1238; a new 1239-1242 keyframe holds Ujście and Nakło only (an empty keyframe is the alternative); the 1241 contest and 1243 gain cover Poznań and Gniezno. The earlier remark that the pages are silent on 1238-1239 was wrong for these two pages. (2) The Seniorate region now excludes Cliopatria's 29 Kuyavia cells in every Seniorate event and in the 1173 and 1228 keyframes. (3) Kuyavia 1199: counterpart is duchy-of-kuyavia, shared with the Masovia dossier. (4) Wieluń (9 cells) is drawn from 1249 to 1304; no page gives its loss; Cliopatria draws it under Sandomierz and Duchies of Poland, so a double-draw remains for the colour agent.
